newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end down in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end down in light trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished marginally lower on Friday as the market groped for direction after the long New Year holidays although there was some moderate buying seen for RSS3 rubber, dealers said.
Volume for the RSS3 February contract reached over 2,600 tonnes. The volume for the other months were slim, dealers said.
"Somebody bid for RSS3 rubber, but aside from that the overall volume in the market remained thin coming out of the New Year holidays," a rubber trader said.
The rubber market was closed last Wednesday for the New Year holiday and on Thursday for Singapore's general elections.

"The market will take its cue from Japan when it finally opens next week, but the near-term direction of the market is hard to forecast," another dealer said. The Japanese rubber market was closed for the entire week.
At around 0945 GMT, February RSS3 was seen at 123.50-125.50 U.S. cents a kg from last Tuesday's settlement of 125.50 cents.
February RSS1 was seen at 176.00-178.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.27) a kg from the previous 178.00 cents.
March TSR20 was seen at 170.00-172.00 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.23) a kg from 173.00 cents.
